examples.name: Sample — threat-report-2025_p29
paragraphs: Every tile prints its label and share: eight rows in reading order, left to right and top to bottom. The percent sign is printed raised beside each number and is written as a superscript. All tile text is set in a heavier weight.

examples.name: Sample — crypto_usage_report2024_p33
paragraphs: Eight tiles, every label copied whole, parenthesis and all. Seven print a number and the eighth, Social, prints <1% — a comparator, not a value. Its row keeps the printed <1%; no value is estimated from the sliver it draws. The footer's logo, copyright line and page number are elided.

examples.name: Sample — apport_p19
paragraphs: Both layers on one page: every state prints its seat count, and the fill classes its change, so each state's row holds both — 50 states. Five states are shown, then the rest; the DE 1 callout on a leader line is read like any other. Delaware's fill is too small to compare with the swatches, so its class cell is empty. The agency footer is elided.

examples.name: Sample — cdc_p3
paragraphs: No values anywhere — state abbreviations printed, six legend classes, no legend title. Each region takes its class: every state, DC and territory shown (about 53 regions). Four regions spread across the classes are shown, then the rest. The legend draws ≥35% as a > glyph over an underline bar; ≥35% is the reading, and a checker treats >35% as the same class. The source lines are cut off at the page edge and are elided.

examples.name: Counter-sample — regional-catastrophe-report-2023_p54
paragraphs: Event pins over a regional map, each callout naming an event and describing its losses (Eco: USD1.9bn / Ins: USD240mn). The map's shading has no discrete legend to class regions against, and a pin's position is not a value, so the map gives no chart table: its printed text is transcribed as text. The data of this page is the loss chart beside the map, which is a chart table like any other; its bars print no values, so they are estimates on the 20-unit grid. The map's title, callouts and place names are elided.
